ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 et seq. and R561-1 et seq. of the French Code monétaire et financier (CMF), in particular Article L561-45 on beneficial-owner identification; Loi n°2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Décret n°2017-1180 of 17 July 2017; Décret n°2019-133 of 27 February 2019; Articles R123-46 to R123-52 of the French Code de commerce; EU Directive 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed; directly applicable EU sanctions regulations; FATF 40 Recommendations for AML/CFT compliance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation and board resolution approving the French SAS investment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry and notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction of organisation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarized power of attorney for French incorporation filings and execution of the SAS statuts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notaire or notary public in the shareholder's country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft SAS Articles of Association (Statuts) including the beneficial-owner declaration schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and first President of the SAS; French notaire if real property contribution is made

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity and address evidence of each ultimate beneficial owner and the SAS President
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing civic authorities in the country of residence or nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds evidence and bank reference letters for shareholders making capital contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's bank or licensed professional services firm

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory electronic screening of every shareholder, UBO, legal representative, President and authorised agent against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU-SANCT), the French national financial sanctions and embargo measures administered by the Direction générale du Trésor and TRACFIN, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for any United States or USD nexus. Politically exposed persons are identified under Article L561-10 CMF; PEP status, family members and close associates automatically trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval. The defense-tactical sector is treated as high risk; the full corporate chain must be pierced through holding vehicles, trusts, nominees, bearer instruments and fiduciary arrangements to each natural-person UBO.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Formalités des entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for filing and Guichet unique processing; INPI national company data and RCS priority-search dashboard (https://data.inpi.fr) for official name-clearance verification.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the mandatory language of corporate filings under the Loi Toubon of 4 August 1994. The SAS name must be expressed in Latin-script characters; any non-Latin script name must be transliterated into standard Latin orthography and accompanied by a certified French translation. The selected name must be distinctive, lawful, non-misleading, available in the RCS and INPI search index, and compliant with French public-order and protected-profession restrictions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide a general renewable administrative name-reservation permit. The INPI/RCS priority-search certificate remains usable for 30 days. Upon a reasoned refusal, the applicant may file a recours gracieux with the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or with INPI within two months, followed by a hierarchical appeal to the Director General of INPI. A final refusal may be appealed before the competent judicial court within one month of notification. The applicant may simultaneously re-file using a revised distinctive suffix and obtain a fresh priority-search certificate; rejection does not confer a right to fee reimbursement.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office or as the principal operational facility for this defense-sector SAS. A physical French head office with document storage, executive presence and export-control compliance records is required before ministerial approval will be considered. A virtual address may be used only for ancillary administrative correspondence and does not satisfy the real-office requirement under Article L210-1 of the French Code de commerce.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very high. Quantified risk of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months is approximately 85%, based on the armored military and tactical vehicle classification, Ministry of the Armed Forces oversight, customs and export-control supervision by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects, and French AML/CFT sectoral risk assessment.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SAS incorporation announcements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for bilingual mid-market SAS incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for institutional-grade screening and reporting.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Defense counsel / former Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for preliminary French defense procurement and export-control advisory.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II — Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), L.210-1 to L.210-10 (formation of commercial companies), R.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); defense manufacturing and trade licensed under the Code de la Défense, Articles L.2331-1 to L.2331-15 and R.2331-1 to R.2331-5; classified installations (ICPE) under the Code de l'Environnement, Articles L.511-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés — RCS) of the registered-office jurisdiction; filings are made exclusively through the INPI Guichet Unique, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, operated with the CCI (Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société (former CERFA M0) submitted electronically via the Guichet Unique, verified by the RCS registrar and evidenced by the Extrait Kbis
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS (Art. L.227-2 Code de commerce); capital is freely set in the statuts, must be fully subscribed by the shareholders, and the paid-in portion must be deposited in a dedicated blocked account held by a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations pending registration, with the bank's 'certificat de dépôt des fonds' or the notary's attestation attached to the filing. For defense procurement and DGA vetting, a paid capital in the order of EUR 500,000 or more is commercially expected, although the law imposes no floor.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [•] SAS. The shareholder resolves as follows: (1) the attached articles of association are approved and [•] SAS is constituted with share capital of EUR [•], represented by [•] shares, fully subscribed and paid-in; (2) the capital is acknowledged as deposited and blocked with [bank], whose blocked-funds certificate is attached; (3) the registered office is fixed at [address] until otherwise decided; (4) [•] is appointed Président, with full power to act towards third parties, open bank mandates, publish the legal notice, complete all RCS formalities and apply for defense, environmental and industrial authorizations. All delegated acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Statuts and Blocking of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire (optional but recommended) and French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all shareholders execute the SAS statuts before a notaire if a real-estate contribution is made or notarization is preferred; wire or transfer the subscribed capital to a dedicated blocked funds account (compte bloqué); obtain the bank's attestation or the notaire's 'attestation de dépôt des fonds' evidencing payment until registration.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts with share distribution and corporate purpose covering ISIC 3040 armored tactical vehicle manufacturing
Bank blocked-funds certificate (certificat de dépôt des fonds)
Notarized attestation if applicable
Identification of all shareholders and the President
Extrait n° 3 of the criminal record (bulletin n° 3) of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the block account, use the CDC or a notarial deposit facility; if the statuts are returned by the notaire for correction, re-sign the rectified version; all corrections are made before any public filing to avoid exposure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Incorporation Notice (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) accredited in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the incorporation notice specifying the corporate name, legal form SAS, amount of capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, name of the President, and the RCS registry; request the JAL issued 'attestation de parution' to be attached to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Draft avis de constitution text
Attestation de parution issued by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL publication is challenged for missing mandatory information, republish an amended notice and obtain a second attestation; the registrar may otherwise reject the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Declaration to the RCS via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online 'déclaration de constitution de société personne morale' (M0-equivalent) with the corporate details, upload the statuts and supporting documents, pay the registry fee of EUR 37.02, and submit; monitor the portal until the greffe issues the certificate of registration or a completion query.
required_dossiers: Filed and signed statuts
Blocked funds certificate or notaire attestation
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Proof of registered office (bail or domiciliation agreement)
Identity documents of shareholders and President
Déclaration de non-condamnation (DNC)
List of the persons authorized to bind the company (pouvoirs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues a 'demande de renseignements' or rejects, cure the deficiency on the Guichet Unique within 10 to 30 days; a formal refusal may be challenged before the supervising judge of the tribunal de commerce under Article R.123-4 Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Extrait Kbis and Automatic Post-Registration Enrollments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE (SIRENE); URSSAF / social security bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the certified Extrait Kbis evidencing legal personality and the SIREN number; verify that the Guichet Unique has automatically completed the INSEE enrollment and the URSSAF declarations; if the company has no employees, file the zero-staff declaration and, within 8 days, register any President assimilated to a salarié for social coverage.
required_dossiers: Certified Extrait Kbis and SIRET numbers
SIRENE enrollment notice from INSEE
URSSAF zero-employee or employer enrollment
Insurance certificates (RC Pro, corporate liability)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is not delivered despite approval, formally request rectification from the greffe; persistent omissions by INSEE are corrected by direct application to the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Defense Manufacturing Authorization (Autorisation de Fabrication de Matériels de Guerre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère des Armées — Direction Générale de l'Armement (DGA), Defense Export and Procurement Authorizations Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the manufacturing authorization application under Articles L.2331-2 and R.2331-3 of the Code de la Défense, describing the all-terrain armored security personnel transport vehicle, technical specifications, production site, security classification of the facilities (zone protégée / IRIS), and the European Union transfer / export compliance framework (Directive 2009/43/EC and Regulation 2021/821); undergo the inter-ministerial assessment and await the ministerial decision.
required_dossiers: DGA application and annexes (technical manual of the armored vehicle)
Extrait Kbis and SIREN
Industrial security program and protection plan (PPST)
Facility access list and security-cleared personnel dossiers
Compliance policy for export licenses and sensitive dual-use items
Proof of financial capacity and insurance for defense liabilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGA issues an incompleteness report, respond within 90 days; a refusal of authorization can be challenged by a hierarchical appeal (recours gracieux) to the Ministre des Armées, then within 2 months before the Tribunal Administratif de Paris.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental (ICPE) Registration and Civil Defense / Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DREAL of the region where the plant is located; Prefect; Commission Consultative Départementale de Sécurité et d'Accessibilité (CCDSA) and SDIS fire service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the ICPE registration dossier (CERFA 15784*02) or full authorization dossier (CERFA 16833*04) if painting, surface treatment or hazardous-waste thresholds are exceeded; prepare an environmental compliance plan covering VOC emissions, industrial wastewater, waste streams and noise; obtain the fire safety inspection certificate; carry out the OPC structural verification for all storage areas and secured production lines.
required_dossiers: ICPE informational questionnaire and compliance plan
EIA or simplified impact study (Art. R.122-2 Code de l'Environnement)
Fire safety dossier and SDIS visit report
OTR structural load certificate
VOC and wastewater monitoring program
Occupational health plan and ATEX zoning dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DREAL emits supplementary prescriptions, implement them within the notified deadline; a refusal or prescription can be challenged before the Prefect and then the Tribunal Administratif; failure to comply subjects the site to a mise en demeure and, ultimately, suspension under Articles L.171-6 to L.171-10 Code de l'Environnement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère des Armées — Direction Générale de l'Armement (DGA) jointly with the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE, Ministry of the Economy) for the defense-industry status and manufacturing authorization
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de fabrication de matériels de guerre (defense manufacturing authorization) under Article L.2331-2 of the Code de la Défense, with additional transfer/export licenses required on first delivery under Directive 2009/43/EC

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique — Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR) and DREAL (inspection des installations classées)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Enregistrement) under the ICPE regime for assembled-vehicle production; upgrade to Authorization (Autorisation) with a full EIA when surface-treatment, painting or volatile-solvent consumption exceeds the thresholds of Article R.511-9 Code de l'Environnement; prototype laboratories may qualify for exemption below de minimis thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: ICPE ministerial limit-values: industrial wastewater pH 5.5-8.5, temperature ≤ 30°C, suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L; VOC emissions capped at 150 mg C/m³ in exhaust air from painting lines; hazardous wastes (paint sludge, cutting fluids, contaminated packaging) must be removed with a bordereau de suivi des déchets dangereux and delivered to licensed treatment plants; noise limits 60 dB(A) at the property boundary during daytime.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the SDIS through the Commission Consultative Départementale de Sécurité et d'Accessibilité (CCDSA) covering fire compartments, extinguishing systems, and egress; OPC (organisme de contrôle technique) structural and load inspection certificate; occupational risk prevention and medicine-at-work clearance under the Code du travail including ATEX zone classification, ventilation controls, and annual medical monitoring for the assembly workforce.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); online corporate portal at impots.gouv.fr; local VAT registration desks are the Services des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); customs and EORI matters are administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent or non-resident shareholder forms the French SAS and registers it at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr single electronic window, obtaining the SIREN and SIRET numbers. The SIE then allocates the intra-Community French VAT identification number and, for employers, the URSSAF registration. For a foreign entity, including a non-resident SAS without a French fixed establishment, making its first taxable supply, a direct VAT registration is filed under Article 289A CGI with the non-resident SIE; EU-established sellers may file directly, while non-EU sellers must appoint a tax representative approved by the DGFiP. The exporter also requires an EORI number beginning with 'FR' for customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A French SAS is a commercial company with full legal personality and is, by default, subject to the standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the entity level under Articles 206(1) and 219 CGI. It is tax-resident in France because it is incorporated and managed in France; no check-the-box pass-through status is available under French tax law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The main available elections are (i) group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Articles 223 A to 223 U CGI where the French parent holds at least 95% of the SAS; (ii) the régime mère-fille dividend exemption under Article 145 CGI if the SAS holds at least 10% of the paying subsidiary; (iii) a French VAT group election for closely-linked taxable persons; and (iv) standard loss carryforward and depreciation elections. There is no affirmative hybrid-mismatch 'check-the-box' election; hybrid mismatches are neutralised automatically under Article 212 bis CGI and are documented for the annual tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mainland France: EUR 85,000 for principal supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for principal supplies of services under Article 293B CGI, with periodic DGFiP revalorisation. A taxable person established outside France has no quantitative threshold: registration is required from the first taxable transaction carried out in France, subject to applicable reverse-charge or distance-selling exceptions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured e-invoicing for B2B and B2C transactions and e-reporting via certified dematerialisation platforms. From 1 September 2026, large and mid-size businesses, and from 1 September 2027, all businesses must issue e-invoices using Factur-X or an equivalent PEPPOL-compatible structure. The Public Invoicing Portal (PPF) carries out near-real-time tax clearance and transaction-data audit; no paper fiscal stamp is required, but every invoice receives a unique technical identifier and must be transmitted to DGFiP through a registered PDP or the PPF. Foreign suppliers without a French establishment must operate through a registered PDP or a French tax representative for e-reporting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods from mainland France to destinations outside the European Union are eligible for the 0% VAT rate under Article 262(I) CGI if (i) the seller is a VAT-registered French taxable person, (ii) the goods are physically transported out of the EU under a customs export declaration, and (iii) documentary proof of export and receipt is obtained within the statutory period. Supplies of services physically performed or enjoyed outside the EU may also be zero-rated under Article 259C CGI where the B2B place-of-supply rules allocate the service outside France. Defense tactical vehicles require a prior French export authorisation issued by the Ministry for the Armed Forces under the Code de la défense, but that authorisation does not replace the VAT conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated customs export declaration from the DELTA/DAC environment (Déclaration d'Exportation / SAD)
EORI certificate and export licence issued under Article L2335-3 Code de la défense for military tactical hardware
Original transport document proving physical movement to the non-EU consignee (Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR)
Commercial invoice containing the export VAT code and zero-rating basis
Packing list and certificate of origin supporting customs valuation and classification
Inward remittance certificate / bank transfer proof evidencing payment by the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and the DGDDI jointly audit export zero-rating claims. The zero rate is provisional until the exporter has supplied full documentary evidence; on failure, VAT is clawed back with French late-payment interest (intérêt de retard). Penalties under Article 1729 CGI are 40% for deliberate inaccuracy or omission and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvre; bad-faith cases may extend the ordinary 3-year limitation period to 6 years, and criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI may apply. For defence goods, an unauthorised export triggers customs smuggling sanctions and suspension or cancellation of the export authorisation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the national central bank and French representative of the European Central Bank (ECB); foreign exchange policy is primarily harmonised at EU level under the eurozone framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. France maintains no exchange-control restrictions on cross-border payments within the EU/EEA. For non-EU counterparties, capital movements are theoretically free, but transactions related to defence equipment, armored vehicles, and military tactical hardware are subject to restrictive licensing, prior authorisation for inward direct investment in sensitive defence sectors, and comprehensive EU sanctions screening. Profit remittances are permitted without a special FX licence, but dividends must satisfy French corporate tax rules, documentary evidence of distributable reserves, and, if applicable, the parent-subsidiary directive requirements to reduce or avoid withholding tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in France. Export proceeds may be retained in euro or foreign currency accounts, subject to Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting for any cross-border transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000, submitted through an authorised intermediary bank within the monthly reporting cycle. Non-compliance with reporting obligations may result in administrative penalties and heightened AML scrutiny.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Trade Finance/LC Facility
Operational Account and FX Hedging Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for non-French licensed digital EMIs, and Medium only for French-licensed or EU-passported electronic money institutions that offer corporate IBANs. Legal constraints: a French SAS may lawfully hold funds with an EMI, but cross-border digital EMIs without a licensed French or EU establishment are generally unsuitable for high-risk defence-sector treasury operations because they cannot provide the full documentary trail, defence-trade due diligence, and sanctions-screening infrastructure required by the AML/CTF framework. Most mainstream fintechs also refuse businesses operating under ISIC 3040/NAICS 336992 due to their internal weapons and military-application exclusion policies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/CTF obligations impose a strict know-your-client process on credit institutions; for high-risk defence-tactical-hardware entities, a physical interview is effectively mandatory. Directors or authorised signatories with at least a 25% ownership or control interest must usually appear at the bank's France office or before a duly appointed agent, produce original identification, and evidence of registered office. Pure remote opening may only be possible for existing EU companies with straightforward public-file structures and no defence nexus, which is not the case here; therefore plan for a physical KYC interview in France or at a French consulate-backed notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Combat-vehicle manufacture classified as high-risk under defence-sector AML frameworks; potential exposure to arms embargo and sanctions violations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid French or EU manufacturing/export licence (e.g., DGA export authorisation, EU general export authorisation or specific licence), end-user certificates, freight-forwarder undertakings, no-sanctions declarations, and a written compliance policy mapping all products to permitted final end-users only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity involving foreign qualified investors or shared control of the non-resident parent entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register extract from the French commercial registry (RCS), a notarised legal structure chart, shareholders' register, identity documents for each ultimate beneficial owner, and evidence of the source of funds/capital for each shareholder.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection uses the SWIFT network with ISO 20022 message types (pain.001 customer credit transfer initiated through the remitting bank; MT103 for correspondent advice). The transfer must state an appropriate purpose code consistent with an equity capital contribution or shareholder loan, such as 'Capital – participation in an enterprise' under the ECB Balance of Payments classification. For non-EU origins, the receiving French bank will require a copy of the share subscription agreement, the SAS afkk/board resolution approving the capital increase, proof of deposit into a blocked capital account if statutory capital is being formed, and the not-arrears/declaration from the notary where applicable. The bank will file the mandatory Banque de France external position/reporting declaration if the amount reaches EUR 50,000 or more. All wires must pass sanctions screening before acceptance; funds originating from or channelled through embargoed jurisdictions will be frozen and reported to TRACFIN and the Direction Générale du Trésor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for armoured-vehicle manufacturing, spare parts, or military tactical systems should use documented SWIFT MT103 payments for low-touch recurring disbursements, SWIFT MT202 for bank-to-bank treasury transfers, and commercial letters of credit (typically irrevocable documentary credits issued under UCP600, transmitted via MT700/MT707) for high-value authenticated long-cycle export contracts. The payment instruction must include the relevant trade description, the DGA licence references, underlying invoices (T1 declaration when moving goods within the EU, EX-A customs declaration for exports outside the EU), and the exact goods nomenclature (HS 8710 or relevant national tariff line). For high-risk defence sales, paying and receiving banks will screen both counterparty and delivered item against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UK and US OFAC sanctions lists where USD-clearing occurs, and prohibited-destination restrictions; if a discrepancy is found, the payment may be rejected, blocked, or reported to TRACFIN under French AML law.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-date EUR/USD forward contracts (onshore deliverable forwards concluded with a French or EU-authorised credit institution)
EUR/USD European-style options and options collars
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD) for medium-term balance-sheet hedging of shareholder loans or capital repayments

Non-deliverable forwards only for a narrow band of inconvertible emerging-market currencies where an underlying trade invoice is denominated in that restricted currency and the French bank confirms the hedge is permitted under its internal risk policy
Interest rate swaps combined with FX swaps in the context of financing for forward-sale contracts, subject to the same clearing and margin rules under EMIR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (balance sheet, income statement, notes) together with statutory auditor's report if audit is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; the shareholders' ordinary general meeting must be convened within six months after fiscal year-end (absolute filing deadline: seven months after fiscal year-end, e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file renders the president or manager liable to a civil fine of up to EUR 2,000 and the company to EUR 4,000; repeated non-compliance can lead to a court-ordered compulsory filing and, ultimately, judicial strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form 2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – online filing at impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal years ending 31 December, the return is due by the second business day after 1 May (e.g., 3 May 2025 for FY 2024); for off-calendar fiscal years, within three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic surcharge on the corporate income tax assessed (reduced to 5% if filed after a formal reminder) plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; repeated failure after formal notice can escalate to a 40% penalty and criminal enforcement for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business property tax declaration and payment (Contribution Foncière des Entreprises – CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due by mid-December each year (actual date announced annually by DGFiP; typically 15 December); the prior year's return establishes the basis and must be consistent with the real property leased or owned for industrial/defence production
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-payment incurs a 10% surcharge plus late-payment interest; failure to file the underlying declaration results in a fixed penalty of EUR 100 per missing asset declaration, plus collection by enforced recovery procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor ('commissaire aux comptes') for an SAS if at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at the balance-sheet date: total assets greater than EUR 4.5 million; net turnover greater than EUR 9 million; average permanent workforce greater than 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory when the SAS controls another undertaking or forms a parent-subsidiary group requiring consolidation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, regulation ANC 2014-03) for individual statutory accounts; consolidated financial statements may apply IFRS in accordance with EU Regulation 1606/2002.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) must be filed with the RCS registry upon incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership. There is no separate annual UBO return; however, during the annual accounts deposit, the company implicitly certifies the continuing accuracy of its UBO data. For share transfers, the SAS must file a modified RCS dossier (including the updated register of shareholders) within one month of the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Securities (Article L228-1 Code de commerce) – records all share issuances, transfers, and shareholder identities
Minute book of shareholders' written consultations and collegial decisions (ordinary and extraordinary resolutions)
Register of beneficial owners – a current copy of the filed UBO declaration retained for inspection

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard IS rate (fiscal years ending on/after 1 Jan 2022).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME reduced rate of 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable profit (turnover ceiling €10 million); R&D tax credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100 million (5% above); innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% up to €400,000; Young Innovative Company (JEI) exemption – 100% IS exemption for the first three profitable years, 50% for the following two; territoriality principle – foreign PE profits generally outside French corporate base, subject to tax treaties and anti-abuse rules; CVAE abolished as of 1 Jan 2024.
